activities.name: Zona Colonial Walking Tour
activities.description: Explore the oldest continuously inhabited European settlement in the Americas — wandering the cobblestoned Calle Las Damas, the Alcázar de Colón palace, and the Cathedral Primada de América, the first cathedral built in the New World, all built from local coral stone in the early 1500s.

activities.name: Los Tres Ojos Limestone Caves
activities.description: Descend into a series of spectacular open-air limestone caverns housing three distinct, iridescent freshwater lagoons — each a different shade of jade and turquoise — plus a secret fourth lake accessed by wooden raft through a narrow cave passage.

activities.name: Faro a Colón — Columbus Lighthouse Museum
activities.description: Tour the massive cross-shaped concrete Columbus Lighthouse monument — housing a museum with exhibits contributed by nations worldwide alongside the reputed tomb of Christopher Columbus — with a powerful laser array projected from its roof visible for miles at night.

activities.name: Boca Chica & Andrés Beach Day
activities.description: Spend a half-day at the shallow, turquoise, reef-protected natural lagoon of Boca Chica — one of the calmest swimming beaches in the Caribbean, with warm flat water rarely exceeding chest depth, perfect for relaxing and eating whole fried snapper from the beachside shacks.
activities.duration_note: Free beach access; bring cash for food and drinks at beachside shacks

activities.name: Cueva de las Maravillas Taíno Cave Art
activities.description: Walk illuminated pathways through an ancient, immaculately preserved cave system to view hundreds of authentic Taíno Indian petroglyphs and pictographs — carved and painted by the indigenous people of Hispaniola over 500 years before Columbus arrived.
activities.location: San Pedro de Macorís, Santo Domingo

activities.name: La Bandera & Mangú Dominican Street Food
activities.description: Eat like a Dominican — La Bandera Dominicana (the national lunch of white rice, red beans, and stewed chicken or beef) at a local comedor like Villar Hermanos, then track down a street vendor for a Chimichurri (a juicy Dominican-style burger topped with shredded cabbage and signature mayo-ketchup sauce).

activities.name: Pescado Frito con Tostones — Beachside Fry Shack
activities.description: Pull up a plastic chair at a beachside fry shack in Boca Chica for the quintessential Dominican coastal meal — a whole red snapper heavily seasoned with garlic and Dominican oregano, fried crispy whole, served with twice-fried tostones plantain discs and a cold Presidente.
activities.duration_note: Always verify seafood price by weight before ordering

activities.name: Bonyé at San Francisco Monastery Ruins
activities.description: Every Sunday night, the atmospheric ruins of the 16th-century San Francisco Monastery transform into Bonyé — a massive, free open-air concert where locals and visitors dance authentic live merengue, Afro-Dominican son, and bachata under the stars inside the roofless coral-stone walls.

activities.name: Plaza de España Terrace Cocktails
activities.description: Settle into the open-air terraces surrounding the illuminated Plaza de España for sunset and evening cocktails — one of the most beautiful public squares in the Caribbean, flanked by colonial palaces and overlooking the Ozama River with a sophisticated, social atmosphere.

activities.name: Isla Saona Catamaran Cruise
activities.description: Board a speedboat to a surreal natural infinity pool in the open ocean — waist-deep water stretching to the horizon, carpeted with starfish — then sail by catamaran to the pristine white sands of Isla Saona, a protected island reserve at the southeastern tip of the Dominican Republic.
activities.duration_note: Book through established operators only — avoid unregistered beach touts

activities.name: Hoyo Azul Cenote Swim at Scape Park
activities.description: Hike a lush rainforest trail inside Scape Park to reach Hoyo Azul — a breathtaking, perfectly circular natural limestone cenote filled with impossibly vivid neon-blue water, surrounded by vertical cliffs draped in tropical vegetation.

activities.name: Playa Macao Surf Session
activities.description: Drive past the resort corridor to Playa Macao — one of the few undeveloped, raw public beaches in Punta Cana, with consistent ocean swells and an active surf camp offering lessons and board rentals on the only real surf break in the eastern region.
activities.duration_note: Free if you have your own board; cost covers lesson and rental

activities.name: Indigenous Eyes Ecological Reserve
activities.description: Walk shaded interpretive trails through a private lowland tropical forest protecting 12 freshwater lagoons formed inside ancient limestone sinkholes — several open for swimming in their clear, cool waters amid resident turtles and tropical birds.

activities.name: Montaña Redonda Mountaintop Swing
activities.description: Ride a rugged 4x4 safari truck up a steep dirt track to a breezy mountaintop platform overlooking the Atlantic Ocean and two shimmering lagoons simultaneously, then swing out on the famous giant mountaintop swings dangling over the dramatic panoramic drop.

activities.name: Langosta a la Parrilla & Mamajuana Tasting
activities.description: Escape the resorts to eat grilled Caribbean spiny lobster at a rustic beach shack at Playa Macao or a local comedor in El Cortecito, then taste Mamajuana — the iconic Dominican cured drink made from rum, red wine, honey, tree bark, and herbs steeped together in a shared bottle.

activities.name: Imagine Cave Nightclub
activities.description: Dance inside one of the world's most unique nightclub venues — Imagine is built entirely within a network of real natural cave systems, with stalactites hanging over the dancefloor, multiple underground chambers playing different music genres, and lasers bouncing off the raw cave walls.

activities.name: Humpback Whale Watching in Samaná Bay
activities.description: Board an eco-certified boat into the protected waters of Samaná Bay to witness thousands of Atlantic humpback whales breaching, tail-slapping, and nursing their calves — the largest annual humpback whale congregation in the North Atlantic, all happening within sight of the shoreline.
activities.duration_note: Seasonal: mid-January through late March only

activities.name: Salto El Limón Waterfall Trek
activities.description: Journey through dense tropical jungle by foot or horseback to reach the spectacular Salto El Limón — a 40-meter waterfall thundering into a natural swimming pool in the heart of the Samaná rainforest, surrounded by royal palms and tree ferns.
activities.duration_note: Hiking on foot is permitted — horseback is optional, not mandatory despite local pressure

activities.name: Los Haitises National Park Boat Tour
activities.description: Speed through the extraordinary Los Haitises — a protected coastal park of densely forested limestone mogote islands, hidden mangrove channels, and sea caves decorated with Taíno cave drawings, inhabited by magnificent frigatebirds, manatees, and howler monkeys.
activities.duration_note: Authorized guide and boat captain required — usually included in tour price

activities.name: Playa Rincón Untouched Beach Day
activities.description: Navigate to the massive, pristine 3-mile crescent beach of Playa Rincón — consistently ranked among the Caribbean's most beautiful — where a cold, crystal-clear freshwater river flows through coconut palms and meets the turquoise sea at the far end.
activities.duration_note: Free access — requires boat or 4x4 transport to reach

activities.name: Playa Frontón Wilderness Boat Trip
activities.description: Hire a local barka fishing boat from Las Galeras to reach the utterly remote Playa Frontón — a wild, untouched beach framed by a dramatic 100-meter vertical black limestone cliff wall, accessible only by sea, with snorkeling reefs and total isolation.

activities.name: Pescado con Coco & Pan de Coco — Samaná Coast
activities.description: Taste the culinary soul of Samaná — fresh catch of the day simmered in a rich, savory coconut, tomato, and garlic reduction (Pescado con Coco), paired with dense, sweet-savory Pan de Coco baked fresh in clay ovens. The millions of coconut palms here make this the definitive version in the country.

activities.name: Pueblo de los Pescadores Beachfront Bar Crawl
activities.description: Stroll the Pueblo de los Pescadores in Las Terrenas — a row of historic wooden fishing shacks transformed into chic Euro-Caribbean beach bars — moving fluidly from barefoot cocktails at Mosquito Beach Bar with smooth bachata to open-air electronic music venues as the night deepens.

activities.name: 27 Waterfalls of Damajagua Canyoning
activities.description: Canyon through a spectacular limestone gorge — sliding down natural smooth-rock chutes, leaping from cliff-top jump platforms, and swimming through deep turquoise pools carved by millions of years of rushing water. Choose the 7, 12, or all 27-waterfall route based on your fitness level.
activities.duration_note: Life jacket and helmet mandatory — certified community guide required. All 27 requires strong swimming ability

activities.name: Puerto Plata Cable Car — Mount Isabel de Torres
activities.description: Ride the only aerial cable car in the entire Caribbean up the lush face of Mount Isabel de Torres to botanical gardens and a Christ the Redeemer statue at the summit — go early for clear views over Puerto Plata and the Atlantic coast before daily clouds roll in by midday.
activities.duration_note: Go by 8:30 AM — cloud cover typically blocks views by midday

activities.name: Cabarete Kiteboarding Lesson
activities.description: Take a hands-on introduction lesson or rent gear at Kite Beach in Cabarete — the undisputed kiteboarding capital of the Caribbean, where consistent thermal trade winds blow across a long, shallow bay creating near-perfect conditions for learning one of the world's most exhilarating wind sports.
activities.duration_note: Best wind: June to August and February to April

activities.name: Fortaleza San Felipe Historic Fortress
activities.description: Tour the imposing 16th-century Spanish coral-stone fortress built to protect the northern coastline from relentless pirate raids — one of the oldest military fortifications in the Americas, later used as a political prison during the Trujillo dictatorship, with a small but fascinating museum inside.

activities.name: Cayo Arena Paradise Island Snorkel Trip
activities.description: Board a speedboat from Punta Rucia to Cayo Arena — a tiny, shifting white sandbar in the middle of the sea, ringed by a beautiful shallow coral reef ecosystem teeming with tropical fish, rays, and sea turtles. One of the most pristine natural snorkeling environments in the country.

activities.name: Chicharrón de Cerdo & Pollo al Carbón
activities.description: Fuel up at a roadside stand for Chicharrón de Cerdo — crispy, intensely seasoned fried pork belly sold by the pound — or find a wood-fired chicken rotisserie for Pollo al Carbón, served with yuca and pickled red onions. Stop in Imbert for a taste of the famous local Geo Queso de Hoja artisanal rolled cheese.

activities.name: Cabarete Beach Strip — Lax Bar & Ojo Club
activities.description: Experience the Caribbean's most relaxed and eclectic beach nightlife — Cabarete's main strip transforms after dark into a continuous open-air party with tables and torches set directly on the sand, bouncing between electronic lounge music at Lax Bar and fast-paced merengue at Ojo Club.

activities.name: Bahía de las Águilas Pristine Beach Expedition
activities.description: Journey to the most remote and untouched beach in the Dominican Republic — a sweeping 8-kilometer arc of blinding white sand inside Jaragua National Park, with no development, no vendors, and water so clear the sandy bottom is visible at 10 meters. Requires a 4x4 and a hired boat.
activities.duration_note: 4x4 vehicle strongly recommended. Bring all food, water, and sun protection — no facilities on the beach

activities.name: Lago Enriquillo Crocodile & Iguana Eco-Cruise
activities.description: Cruise the hypersaline Lago Enriquillo — the lowest point in the Caribbean and the largest lake in the Antilles — to spot massive American crocodiles sunbathing on the shore, rhinoceros iguanas by the hundreds, and flamingo flocks in this extraordinary prehistoric landscape.

activities.name: Balneario San Rafael Mountain River Swim
activities.description: Cool off where a cold, cascading mountain river flows over natural concrete-smooth limestone tiers directly onto a rugged pebble beach at the ocean edge — a beloved local swimming hole where Dominican families gather on weekends to bathe in the rushing freshwater pools.

activities.name: Los Patos River & Beach
activities.description: Wade in the transparent, ice-cold waters of Los Patos — the shortest river in the Antilles — which forms a beautiful freshwater lagoon right beside the ocean, creating a rare natural swimming spot where cold river water and warm Caribbean saltwater meet.

activities.name: Larimar Mines 4x4 Expedition
activities.description: Take a steep, bone-rattling 4x4 track up into the remote Bahoruco mountain range to visit the only mines on Earth producing Larimar — a rare, sky-blue volcanic pectolite stone found exclusively in this single mountain in the Dominican Republic, watched over by small-scale artisan miners.
activities.duration_note: High-clearance 4x4 required for mountain road access

activities.name: Chivo Liniero & Chenchén — Southwest Frontier Feast
activities.description: Taste the most distinctive regional cuisine in the Dominican Republic — Chivo Liniero, an extraordinarily aromatic wild goat stew where the meat is naturally seasoned from the inside by the wild oregano bushes the goats graze on, served with Chenchén, a savory cracked-corn pilaf cooked with milk and spices unique to this region.

activities.name: Barahona Malecón Colmado Night
activities.description: Experience deeply authentic Dominican social life — locals park along the Barahona Malecón sea wall, open their car trunks as impromptu sound systems blasting bachata and dembow, and socialize freely. Buy a cold Presidente from Colmado El Bodegón and join the communal street party under the stars.
